correctness.rationale: With d=r−1 cube bit-flip matrices T_i commuting and squaring to I over F2, B=sum T_i satisfies B²=dI and S=I+B satisfies S²=(r mod2)I. All dual checks are exactly (St,t). Odd r yields S²=I, so dual code is self-orthogonal; two target-containing checks disjoint off the target would have odd intersection, impossible. Even r yields S²=0; systematic symbols are similarly restricted by orthogonality of image vectors St; parity admits disjoint checks for t=e_v and t=Se_v. For even r>=4, rank(S)=N/2, ker S=im S self-orthogonal, and every nonzero image has weight>=4; among k disjoint parity checks at most one has zero image, giving 4(k−1)<=N. For r=4 the explicit hex t=c3,11,09 give three mutually disjoint helper supports, sharp at k=3. Independent exact dual-check enumeration at r=2,3,4 confirmed systematic/parity availability (1,2),(1,1),(1,3) and localities (2,1),(3,3),(4,3). This finite enumeration does not claim exact availability for even r>=6, appropriately left bounded.

value.rationale: A clean parity-dependent obstruction and construction for disjoint linear single-symbol repair in a natural structured code family is of genuine coding-theoretic interest; the r=4 sharp three-way recovery and general even-r upper bound are structural rather than tiny arbitrary brute-force invariants. Exact larger-even availability is honestly left open.

final_claim: For binary systematic codes (x,(I+A(Q_{r−1}))x), linear disjoint recovery availability is 1 for all information symbols, 1 for parity symbols at odd r, and >=2 at even r; at r=2 parity availability is 2 and at r=4 it is 3, with general upper 1+2^(r−3) for even r>=4.
limitations: Only binary linear recovery, the specified systematic coordinate split, and unrestricted helper-set size.
